findings.title: Revalidate native signature ownership when publishing concurrent cold imports
findings.finding: The cold-import ownership check only sees the shared cache at adaptation time. Imported provenance remains attempt-local until terminal commit. Two overlapping singleton requests, under different profiles/routes or conversations, can therefore both accept the same previously unseen signature. After the first commits, the second still publishes its scoped record without rechecking the now-known foreign binding: putBatch checks capacity, and the shared provenance value contains no owner to compare. Both scoped records then pass exact replay. The selection queue does not prevent this: it only runs with explicit context and is keyed per action/agent/route.
findings.impact: The advertised known-owner/conversation rejection is bypassable during concurrent cold imports. This is a local routing-isolation finding; it does not claim that a live provider would accept a foreign signature or that any real credential crossed a boundary.
staticReproduction: Prepare request A for a cold signature in owner/conversation A and pause its upstream before terminal.
Prepare overlapping request B containing the same signature in owner/conversation B while the shared cache is still cold.
Complete A successfully, publishing A and provenance.
Complete B successfully. Its staged commit has no foreign-owner revalidation, so it also publishes B.
Exact later replay in B now finds B scoped state instead of rejecting the known foreign signature.
findings.requestedChange: Make cold-signature adoption atomic across in-flight attempts. Store enough provenance to compare the owning scope, and reserve/serialize imports or reject conflicting publication with rollback for failed/cancelled attempts. If known foreign history must never reach a second upstream, enforce the reservation before dispatch as well as at publication. Add a deterministic deferred-upstream regression covering concurrent distinct owners/conversations, success ordering, and release after rejection/cancellation.
findings.verification: Static control-flow proof only; deliberately not executed under the read-only assignment.
findings.confidence: high for the local concurrency gap; live provider acceptance is unverified

findings.title: Remove live upstream and native credential defaults from the offline HTTP fixture
findings.finding: The fixture replaces only accessProfiles.native.baseUrl with loopback. loadConfig otherwise keeps the production Anthropic/Codex endpoints and default native auth paths, while buildDeps receives no restricted fetch implementation. In particular, if the behavior under test regresses so model work is no longer matched as an explicit route, the production HTTP handler falls through to Anthropic passthrough at the default live endpoint. A route regression can thus make this purportedly offline test contact a vendor rather than just fail locally. The fabricated env map only scopes ProfileAuth; it does not make the entire production dependency graph offline.
findings.impact: Offline/no-vendor-contact isolation is not guaranteed on regression paths. No external request or native credential read was observed or executed by this reviewer.
findings.requestedChange: Configure every reachable legacy/API/subscription/refresh endpoint to fixture-owned loopback origins and all native auth paths to fixture-owned nonexistent files. Add a fetch/network allowlist for the routed path and assertions that unexpected routing reaches only a local rejection fixture. Preserve the existing stream=true/false checks. Do not execute the denied HTTP gate through another session.
findings.verification: Static configuration and server fallthrough inspection only; no network/test execution.
